Paperless Sync is a Nextcloud app that mirrors finished Paperless-ngx documents into a structured archive folder of a Nextcloud user and can submit files from a Nextcloud inbox folder to Paperless. Paperless stays the source of truth. The file names contain the marker `[P<ID>]`, which the companion app Paperless Unified Search (Dennis-Otto/paperless-unified-search) uses to find them. Its users are Nextcloud administrators; many use German folder names, such as `_Gelöscht` for deleted documents.

Where things are:

- The app is in `lib/`: `Service/SyncService.php` runs a synchronization, `Service/PathTemplateService.php` builds the archive paths, `Service/NextcloudStorageService.php` writes the files, `Service/PaperlessApiService.php` talks to Paperless, `Service/SyncStateRepository.php` remembers what was mirrored, `Service/ConfigService.php` and `Model/SyncConfig.php` hold the settings, `Service/StatusService.php` and `Model/SyncReport.php` the status and reports, `Cron/SyncJob.php` the background job, `Controller/` and `Settings/` the administration page. Its metadata, version and supported Nextcloud versions are in `appinfo/info.xml`, the settings page in `templates/`, `js/` and `css/`, the German texts in `l10n/`.
- `README.md` documents the features, the configuration (connection, folder ownership, path template variables, deletion safety, background jobs) and the security; `CHANGELOG.md` lists the changes of every release; `docs/releases.md` the release process.
- The PHPUnit tests are in `tests/Unit/`, the Docker end-to-end tests against real Nextcloud versions in `tests/e2e/`.

What matters in a bug report: the version of the app, the Nextcloud version (Administration settings → Overview), the PHP version, the Paperless-ngx version, the relevant settings (target user, folders, path template, conflict policy, deletion settings), whether a dry run shows the same, the status or error summary of the run, and the relevant lines of the Nextcloud log (Administration settings → Logging), without the Paperless API token, private URLs or document contents.
